name: blog-navigate
narration: The ghost browses the web: Chromium projects the whole DOM into the accessibility tree, so links are named elements with native actions — no pixels, no DOM scraping, no browser driver.
notes: VALIDATED on Windows 11 + Microsoft Edge. Open https://www.jocheojeda.com in Edge first and pass --app pid:<edge>. Gotcha: one Edge process hosts every window, so match names precisely — post-card links contain their whole summary text.

steps.say: Checking the blog home is on screen
Finding tonight's read by name — a link in the accessibility tree, not a box of pixels
Showing the human what the ghost is looking at
Opening the post — native invoke on the link
Verifying the navigation by the new page title
Going back — the browser's own Back button, also just a named element
